C1.rationale: Every hard constraint concerns irreversible data loss (stash/reset/force-remove destroying a coworker's uncommitted work), and each one states the causal why — the asymmetry between committed and untracked work, the cost ratio of leaving a stale worktree vs force-removing a live one — so the model can generalise past the enumerated cases. Where certainty is unavailable the unit hands the call back to judgment rather than prohibiting.

evidence.quote: **Commit early.** Untracked files are the only work a concurrent branch switch / reset can destroy with no recovery path — committed work survives in the reflog, untracked work does not.
When no signal reports a coworker, still prefer explicit paths over bulk staging — the detection is best-effort, not a guarantee.

C2.rationale: The unit is an always-loaded narrative rule with no invocation surface of its own — no arguments, flags, or parameters. It does cite a verdict vocabulary and KEY=VALUE keys, but those are the interface of the git-coworker-check skill's detect-coworkers.sh, not of this file; scoring them here would be judging another artifact's interface.

C3.rationale: The always-loaded entry point carries four full bash implementations (baseline snapshot, /proc process scan, worktree-leak probe loop, bare-flip probe), a taskwarrior UDA table, a recovery table, and a Limitations section — reference detail and rare paths inlined alongside the core invariant. A supporting surface exists and is named (the git-coworker-check skill, hooks-plugin, three related rules), which keeps this above a 1, but none of the deferrable detail was actually deferred.

C4.rationale: git-plugin/skills/git-coworker-check/SKILL.md declares the boundary ('See .claude/rules/agent-coworker-detection.md for the full rationale and signal design') but both surfaces then carry the same bare-flip recovery steps (core.bare false, the GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE override, reflog/fsck/worktree-branch salvage) and a near-verbatim commit-early paragraph. The cost of that copy is already visible inside the unit: its own Integration Points table says 'three signals' while its table six lines earlier enumerates six.

C5.rationale: Roughly two thirds of this always-loaded file is procedure with an explicit trigger — capture a baseline at session start, probe before a destructive op, recover after a bare flip — and that procedure is already owned by an on-demand skill with scripts and tests. Applying the decisive test section by section, the invariants that must hold every turn (never destroy work you did not create; stage explicit paths; never force-remove a worktree you did not create) are a small minority of the tokens. It clears a 1 because the gotchas it does carry (worktree leak, bare flip, the force-remove break) are genuinely non-obvious and could not be read off the repo, but it is far from the 'lightweight, gotchas only' bar.

Before any destructive operation (`stash`, `restore`, `checkout -- .`, `reset --hard`), compare current state against the baseline.

C6.rationale: The deterministic work is genuinely delegated in places — scripts/check-git-sandbox-guards.sh is named as the prevention guard, and the git-coworker-check skill (with its scripts/ and scripts/tests/) is named as the primary surface — and what prose could have described is given as executable shell rather than English. It falls short of exemplary because the runnable detector (detect-coworkers.sh) is never named, the snippets are illustrative re-statements of it rather than an invocation, and the unit never says whether the model should run or read them.

top_finding: Move the six signal implementations, their bash blocks, the bare-flip recovery table and the Limitations caveats into git-plugin/skills/git-coworker-check/REFERENCE.md, leaving the always-loaded rule as the hazard statement, the response invariants, the verdict vocabulary and a named pointer to the skill.
counter_finding: The Response Rules plus the 'never force-remove a worktree you don't own' invariant genuinely must be resident every turn — they fire before any git operation regardless of what the user asked, their violation is unrecoverable peer data loss, and no on-demand skill can be relied on to load first.

leakage.note: This repo auto-injects CLAUDE.md and a large set of .claude/rules/*.md into every turn, so three files the hard constraints forbade reading (skill-quality.md, skill-development.md, skill-evaluation.md) arrived unbidden in a system-reminder, as did the unit under judgment. I did not open them deliberately and did not score against any house standard: the 26,000-char ceiling, the mandatory When-to-Use and Agentic Optimizations tables, the REFERENCE.md filename, the description-length band, the date fields and the positive-framing style all played no part. C3 was scored on disclosure structure (what is inlined vs deferred), not on any character threshold, and C4 was scored from a direct read of git-plugin/skills/git-coworker-check/SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md that I discovered by search. One incidental observation worth recording: the injection itself is evidence for C5 — this ~14KB file demonstrably lands in every agent context in this repo, including judging agents with no git-safety task.
